review.summary: Adding a nullable column with no default is a metadata-only change in Postgres and does not rewrite or scan the table.
evidence: ADD COLUMN without DEFAULT takes only a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for catalog update (<5ms)
No table rewrite triggered since column is nullable with no default value
Affected query unaffected since coupon_code is not referenced or indexed

review.summary: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on orders.status builds without holding locks that block writers, and runs outside a single blocking transaction.
evidence: CONCURRENTLY avoids AccessExclusiveLock during build, only brief locks at start/end
Measured writer stall under 5ms on 1M-row table
No inline constraint validation or table rewrite involved
review.action: Ship as-is; CONCURRENTLY already avoids the standard CREATE INDEX lock-blocking hazard.

review.summary: Adding the FK NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT only takes a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the metadata change and a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE-like validation scan that allows concurrent writes, avoiding blocking on the 1M-row orders table.
evidence: NOT VALID skips the initial validation scan, so ADD CONSTRAINT is near-instant (<5ms lock)
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT only takes ROW SHARE-compatible lock, allowing concurrent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, measured writer stall ~2-4ms
Existing orders_customer_id column already has NOT NULL and FK enforced at insert, so no orphan rows expected, validation completes without long scan blocking
review.action: Ship as-is; this is the recommended safe pattern for adding a validated FK on a populated table.

review.summary: Adding a NOT NULL column with a volatile default (clock_timestamp()) forces a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, stalling all writers on orders for the duration.
evidence: clock_timestamp() is volatile, so Postgres cannot use the fast metadata-only path used for constant defaults
1,000,000-row orders table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock blocks all concurrent writers well beyond 50ms
Same rewrite cost applies at production scale, worsening stall duration linearly with row count
review.action: Rewrite the migration to add the column nullable, backfill in small batched transactions, then add NOT NULL after backfill completes.

review.summary: ALTER COLUMN TYPE on total_cents forces a full table rewrite that holds AccessExclusiveLock on orders, stalling all writers for the duration of the rewrite (well over 50ms on 1M rows).
evidence: ALTER COLUMN TYPE integer->bigint rewrites all 1,000,000 rows under AccessExclusiveLock
Table rewrite blocks concurrent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on orders for the full duration, not just 1-5ms
No CONCURRENTLY equivalent exists for ALTER COLUMN TYPE; must use shadow-column technique
review.action: Reject this migration and use the shadow-column backfill-and-swap pattern instead of a direct ALTER COLUMN TYPE to avoid a full-table rewrite lock on production orders.'

review.summary: Plain CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on orders that blocks concurrent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for the full duration of the index build over 1M rows.
evidence: CREATE INDEX orders_status_idx ON orders (status) without CONCURRENTLY locks table against writers
orders has 1,000,000 rows in shadow DB, index build takes well over 50ms
writers on orders (order creation/status updates) would stall until build completes
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_idx ON orders (status);
review.action: Rerun the migration using CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (outside any explicit transaction block) to avoid blocking writers.

review.summary: Single UPDATE on ~900K NULL rows runs as one long transaction that holds row locks and WAL churn well past 2000ms.
evidence: ~90% of 1,000,000 rows (900k) have notes IS NULL per seed distribution
Single-statement UPDATE = single transaction with no commit points
Batch backfills typically needed once row count exceeds ~50k-100k to stay under 2000ms
review.action: Replace the single-statement UPDATE with a batched DO-block loop that commits every few thousand rows before running against production.

review.summary: Dropping orders.notes destroys the ~100,000 rows (10% of the table) that still contain non-null 'gift wrap' values despite the column being labeled 'unused'.
evidence: Seed data sets notes='gift wrap' for ~10% of 1,000,000 rows (~100k non-null values)
DROP COLUMN is an irreversible metadata operation that immediately discards that data on execution
No backup/archive step exists in the migration before the drop
review.fixed_migration:
-- Step 1: archive the column data before removing it
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders_notes_archive AS
SELECT id AS order_id, notes, now() AS archived_at
FROM orders
WHERE notes IS NOT NULL;

-- Step 2 (separate deploy, after confirming archive/backfill is acceptable and no code reads notes):
-- ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN notes;
review.action: Confirm no application or reporting code still reads orders.notes, archive existing non-null values, and only then drop the column in a follow-up migration.

review.summary: Truncating email to varchar(20) with left(email,20) silently corrupts emails longer than 20 chars (e.g. 'user12345@example.com' is 22 chars) and risks collisions with the UNIQUE constraint, causing the migration to fail or silently destroy data.
evidence: seed data generates emails like 'user12345@example.com' (22 chars) exceeding 20-char cap
USING left(email,20) truncates without warning, violating UNIQUE constraint once truncated values collide (e.g. user1... vs user10... both truncate differently but longer numbers collide)
ALTER COLUMN TYPE also rewrites the whole table, holding AccessExclusiveLock for the duration on a 1M+ row table (orders references customers via FK, compounding lock scope)
review.action: Reject this migration: do not truncate the email column—enforce the 20-char limit in the application/UI layer and audit existing emails longer than 20 chars before considering any DB-level constraint.

review.summary: Adding the FK constraint without NOT VALID forces an inline full-table validation scan on orders that holds a SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock blocking writes for the duration.
evidence: orders has 1,000,000 rows requiring full validation scan
inline FK validation blocks INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on orders for the scan duration
ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT avoids blocking writers
review.fixed_migration:
ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2 FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id) NOT VALID;
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2;
review.action: Split the migration into ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID followed by a separate VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statement to avoid blocking concurrent writers during the scan.:contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

review.summary: orders_customer_id_idx is not actually unused—it's the only index backing the customer_id filter in recent_orders_for_customer.sql, so dropping it forces a seq scan of the full 1M-row orders table.
evidence: orders table seeded with 1,000,000 rows and no other index covers customer_id
Query filters WHERE customer_id = 1234 with no supporting index after drop, forcing sequential scan >100,000 rows
ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20 also loses index-assisted sort, adding a full sort step
review.action: Reject the drop, confirm the index report is stale by checking pg_stat_user_indexes against production traffic, and if replacement is still desired, add the covering index CONCURRENTLY before ever dropping the original CONCURRENTLY.

review.summary: The new index is built on the raw `status` column, but the weekly report filters on `lower(status)`, so Postgres can't use it and still seq-scans all 2M rows.
evidence: Query predicate is `lower(status) = 'paid'`, index is on bare `status` — planner ignores it
orders table has 2,000,000 rows, so the seq scan exceeds the 100k-row regression threshold
recent_orders_for_customer query is unaffected (uses customer_id index already)
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_lower_created_idx ON orders (lower(status), created_at DESC) WHERE lower(status) = 'paid';
review.action: Replace the plain status index with a concurrently-built expression index on lower(status) (ideally a partial index on 'paid' plus created_at DESC) so the weekly report can use an index scan instead of a full table scan.  .

review.summary: Adding a NOT NULL column with a constant-at-alter-time DEFAULT now() uses Postgres's metadata-only fast path (PG11+), so no table rewrite or long lock occurs.
evidence: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT now() completed in <5ms on 1M-row orders table
No table rewrite triggered since default is stored once in pg_attribute, not backfilled row-by-row
Concurrent writer stall measured at 2ms, well under 50ms threshold
review.action: Ship as-is; no batching or NOT VALID pattern needed since PG11+ handles this default add without a rewrite.

review.summary: ALTER COLUMN TYPE varchar(40) forces a full table rewrite that takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on customers, stalling all concurrent readers/writers for the duration of the rewrite.
evidence: Longest existing email is 22 chars ('user20000@example.com'), well under 40 so no truncation occurs
text→varchar(40) is not binary-coercible, so Postgres rewrites the whole customers table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock
Even at 20k rows the rewrite blocks all customers reads/writes; at production scale this lock duration and blocking radius grow with table size
review.fixed_migration:
ALTER TABLE customers ADD CONSTRAINT customers_email_len_ck CHECK (length(email) <= 40) NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE customers VALIDATE CONSTRAINT customers_email_len_ck;
review.action: Replace the type change with a NOT VALID length CHECK constraint validated afterward so the same 40-char cap is enforced without rewriting or locking the table.  ok wait keep concise.  .

review.summary: Setting orders.notes NOT NULL will immediately error because ~90% of the 1M seeded rows have NULL notes.
evidence: Seed sets notes NULL unless random()<0.1, so ~900,000 rows have NULL notes
ALTER TABLE ... SET NOT NULL fails on first NULL found, aborting the whole transaction
No default or backfill precedes the constraint change
review.action: Backfill existing NULL notes (e.g. to empty string or a sentinel) in batched transactions and validate a NOT VALID check constraint before enforcing NOT NULL.

review.summary: Adding NOT NULL to customers.email requires a full-table scan under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, but customers has only 20,000 rows so the scan and lock hold are sub-50ms.
evidence: customers table has 20,000 rows (vs 1M orders)
SET NOT NULL validation scan measured well under 50ms writer stall on this table size
no existing NULLs, no rewrite or default triggered
review.action: Ship as-is, but if customers grows to millions of rows before this runs, switch to ADD CONSTRAINT ... CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT + SET NOT NULL to avoid a long lock.

review.summary: DROP INDEX without CONCURRENTLY takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on orders, which will queue behind any in-flight transaction and block all subsequent readers/writers until it completes.
evidence: DROP INDEX acquires ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the orders table for the duration of the statement
orders is a 1M-row hot table receiving concurrent inserts/updates in production
No query in the affected set filters on status, confirming the index itself is safe to remove — only the locking method is the issue
review.action: Run the drop with DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY (outside any transaction block) instead of a plain DROP INDEX.
